questions.question: Why does Salesforce enforce strict governor limits?
options: To make Apex harder to learn
Because Salesforce is multi-tenant — shared infrastructure must be protected from any one org's runaway code
Governor limits only apply to free Developer Edition orgs
To discourage the use of asynchronous Apex
questions.explanation: Multi-tenancy means many orgs share the same underlying infrastructure — governor limits stop one org's code from degrading performance for everyone else.

questions.question: How many callouts can a single Apex transaction make, according to this course?
questions.explanation: A single transaction can make up to 100 callouts.

questions.question: Why does a callout fail if it happens after uncommitted DML in the same transaction?
options: Salesforce blocks any callout once the transaction has made uncommitted database changes, to prevent inconsistent state
Apex doesn't support DML and callouts in the same class at all
Callouts automatically commit any pending DML first
This is only a problem in sandboxes, not production
questions.explanation: Once a transaction has uncommitted DML, Salesforce blocks further callouts — the fix is usually to do the callout first, then the DML, or move the callout to its own asynchronous transaction.

questions.question: Why should a production integration pin a specific API version in its endpoint URL?
options: Pinning a version is required by law
An unpinned call could see Salesforce's behavior change on a future release; pinning keeps it stable until you deliberately upgrade
Pinning a version makes callouts run without any governor limits
questions.explanation: Pinning a version (e.g. v61.0) protects your integration from unexpected behavior changes introduced in later Salesforce releases.

questions.question: Why can't a trigger make a direct, synchronous callout?
options: Triggers are not allowed to call Apex methods
A trigger's transaction is likely to include uncommitted DML, and no callout is allowed after uncommitted DML in the same transaction
Triggers can only run on weekends
Callouts are disabled by default in all orgs
questions.explanation: Since a trigger's transaction typically includes the DML that fired it, a direct callout would violate the no-callout-after-uncommitted-DML rule — the work has to move to an asynchronous context instead.
